title: In vivo effective trunk stiffness from quick release (35% max exertion) in flexion, extension and lateral bending under vertical and horizontal trunk loads (ACTIVE muscle)
condition: semi-seated, hips restrained, isometric exertion at 35% max force before release (ACTIVE muscle)

quantity.name: effective trunk rotational stiffness K
quantity.definition: second-order model I*theta'' + B*theta' + K*theta = C fitted (double-integrated) to trunk rotation after sudden release of a T9 cable force; I from anthropometry (trunk+head+arms, plus added loads), moment arm L from L4/L5 to T9; includes intrinsic muscle stiffness and possibly early reflex; effective stability = K corrected by gravitational/potential energy terms

source.authors: Cholewicki J, Simons APD, Radebold A
source.sample: 12 healthy subjects without LBP history (6 M, 6 F)

protocol.summary: Semi-seated in a jig restricting hip motion with the upper torso free; chest harness at ~T9 with a cable held by an electromagnet; subject exerted isometric extension, flexion, left or right lateral bending to 35% of max force (release force 172 (54) N), released at random delay; trunk motion recorded at 80 Hz (inductive sensor). Added loads: vertical 0/20/40% BW in harness pouches (COM ~T9), horizontal 0/10/20% BW via cable and bucket, 9 permutations x 4 directions x 3 trials.
how_to_simulate: Semi-seated model with pelvis/hips fixed and upper trunk free; add vertical (0-40% BW at T9) and horizontal (0-20% BW at T9) external loads
Solve muscle activations for an isometric exertion of ~172 N at T9 (35% max) in the given direction plus the external loads, including muscle short-range stiffness

Compute the trunk rotational stiffness about L4/L5 (linearised stiffness of the musculoskeletal system, e.g. from the Hessian/stability analysis) and compare with K (Nm/rad); or simulate the release and fit the second-order model
protocol.notes: ACTIVE: stiffness includes active muscle; never pool with passive tests. Table 1 values are main effects (averaged over the other load factor). Model-based stability index (Table 2) not extracted (model output).
